feedback: Evidence so far: iteration 0 (12 mm, plus/minus 0.024 m) and iteration 1 (12 mm, plus/minus 0.05 m) both ended every run off_track with max_error of about 0.061 m. Widening the span to plus/minus 0.05 m cut line-loss events to 0 on the oval and slalom and to 1 on the s-bend, but max_error and RMS error barely changed (about 0.030 m RMS in both). So coverage was the cause of line loss, not of the excursion. The 0.061 m excursion is probably the controller's steering response, which is weaker with the wider row. Your 16 mm footprint is compatible with the controller I am building, and I am compensating for the weaker signal by raising kp. I make no prediction about how this robot will race. Once its race is in, the next decision depends on its max_error and line-loss counts. If line loss stays at zero and max_error stays near 0.061 m, the next geometry lever is sensor y (look-ahead), not footprint or span. If line loss returns with the 16 mm footprint, hold the footprint and report which track shows it. If steering_oscillation rises markedly, the wider row is not the cause, so hold the controller gain and try a longer look-ahead.
requested_changes: Keep the 16 mm footprint at plus/minus 0.05 m (y = 0.04), since line loss was removed by span in iteration 1; report line_loss_events per track.
If max_error stays near 0.061 m with line loss at zero, try sensor y = 0.06 (longer look-ahead) with the same span and footprint, and report whether max_error moves.
If line loss returns with 16 mm footprints, revert to 12 mm at plus/minus 0.05 m and ask the Integrator for a steering-gain change instead of another geometry change.
